vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: notion-sync
Version: 2.4.0

The skill demonstrates good security practices for API token handling, explicitly warning against exposing credentials in process listings. All network communication is confined to the Notion API, and file system access (reading/writing markdown, state files) is aligned with the skill's stated purpose. However, the skill is vulnerable to path traversal via unsanitized file path arguments. Specifically, `scripts/notion-to-md.js` writes to `outputFile` and `scripts/watch-notion.js` writes to `stateFile` and reads from `localPath` without robust input sanitization. A malicious AI agent or user could exploit this to write to arbitrary file paths (e.g., `../../../../etc/passwd` or `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`), leading to data corruption, denial of service, or potential remote code execution. This constitutes a critical vulnerability, classifying the skill as 'suspicious' rather than 'malicious' as there is no evidence of intentional self-exploitation or malicious design within the skill itself.

llm.summary: The skill's files, runtime instructions, and required credential (NOTION_API_KEY) are coherent with its stated Notion-sync purpose; nothing in the bundle appears to request unrelated secrets or contact unexpected endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included scripts: Node-based utilities to search/query/update Notion and convert to/from Markdown. Required binary (node) and required env var (NOTION_API_KEY) are appropriate for this purpose. Minor metadata quirk: the registry shows no 'primary credential' field while NOTION_API_KEY is required, but that's a metadata omission rather than a functional mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts confine themselves to Notion API calls (api.notion.com), local file I/O for markdown and a local state file, and token resolution (token file, stdin, ~/.notion-token, or NOTION_API_KEY). The scripts read token sources automatically (including ~/.notion-token) and may read stdin (fd 0) when --token-stdin is used — this is expected for credential handling but is worth noting so users choose the token provisioning method they trust.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external install/download step is declared and no remote URLs are fetched; the package is self-contained JS scripts that require Node on PATH. Note: registry metadata says 'instruction-only' but the skill includes code files bundled with the skill (no external installer) — this is not a security red flag but is an inconsistency in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY (and standard Node env) is required. The code reads token from either a token file, stdin, ~/.notion-token, or NOTION_API_KEY — which is reasonable for convenience/automation. The skill does not request unrelated credentials or access other system configuration paths beyond the user-specified state file and token file.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true. The only persistent artifact is an optional per-workspace state file (default memory/notion-watch-state.json) created when using watch-notion.js — expected behavior for a watcher. The skill does not modify other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: operate on Notion via your integration token and local markdown files. Before installing: 1) Only provide a Notion integration token you trust and grant the integration only the workspace/pages it needs. 2) Prefer the token-file option (~/.notion-token with chmod 600) or piping via stdin rather than embedding tokens on command line. 3) Be aware watch-notion.js will create/update a local state file (default: memory/notion-watch-state.json) in the working directory — run it from a directory you control. 4) Confirm you trust the source repo (homepage provided). If you want higher assurance, review the included scripts yourself (they are bundled and readable) before running them.
